answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A relic delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A jade check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A lotus penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 11642 identities need 11642 bonds of 49 tokens, 35942 dollars of hardware and 27 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
